text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak told CNN that Egypt is determined to pursue economic reform until it achieves its aims because the economic reform programme is very important. He said Egypt was working hard to persuade more Egyptians and foreigners to invest because more investment means more production and jobs.

- In an interview with The New York Times, Mubarak said the patience of the Arab man in the street was running out and that Egypt and other Arab countries find themselves pushed into a very difficult situation as long as Israel does not prove it is willing to adapt to Palestinian demands.

- In an interview with the Israeli newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth, Mubarak said that the Israeli Azam Azam, detained in Cairo since November 8, was a spy. He said an Egyptian revealed Azam and that the police found invisible ink on him when they caught him.

- The Middle East economic conference held its closing session under Egyptian Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri, who said we needed a coherent economic bloc like the one in Europe and that Egypt would do its utmost to put the Middle East peace process back on track. The final declaration of the conference said the participants were committed to a just, lasting and comprehensive peace in the Middle East based on the terms of reference of the Madrid conference and U.N. Security Council resolutions 242 and 338.
The declaration stressed the need to speed up implementation of the agreements between all parties.
- Mubarak called the President of the United Arab Emirates, Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan, on Thursday evening to congratulate him of his recovery from recent surgery.

- Electricity Minister Maher Abaza said Egypt turned down a long-term World Bank loan of $350 million for electricity projects. He said the Egyptian electricity sector would rely on domestic finance to carry out new projects.

- The final declaration of the economic summit said all parties must carry out the agreements signed between the Arabs and Israel since the Madrid conference. It also called on all parties to follow a policy of building confidence, continue with economic reform and remove obstacles to trade.
- Mubarak met the president of the European Investment Bank, Sir Brian Unwin, who said he discussed with Mubarak the role the bank can play in the Middle East.

- A dangerous terrorist, Abdennabi Ahmed Ali Hassan, was killed yesterday in southern Egypt. A police force had gone out to arrest him at his hiding place in fields in Minya province but Hassan opened fire at them. The police fired back and killed him. Police believe he was a member of the Gama'a unit which robbed a bank in the southern town of Ayat.
- Strong winds in the Edfu area sank a Nile cruiser carrying 83 Czech and Slovak tourists and 56 Egyptian crew. Six tourists and 18 crew members are still missing.
- Mubarak warned of destruction and terrorism if Israel does not keep in step with moves towards peace in the Middle East.
- A diplomatic source said Egyptian forces would take part in the U.N. force which the Security Council plans to end to Zaire at the request of African leaders.
